programme.desc: One of the most important yet overlooked periods in human history; the who, what, why, where, when and how of the Golden Age of Islamic Civilization; exploring the Abbasid Empire; how it bridged the ancient world and the Renaissance.

programme.title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
programme.desc: Meeting the Moroccan wayfarer Ibn Battuta; tracing his journey across Northern Africa and the Middle East in the century after the Mongol sack of Baghdad; new insights into the era, including whether it ever truly come to an end.

programme.title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
programme.desc: Getting to know Caliph Harun al-Rashid; Baghdad's House of Wisdom, which is the largest depository of books in the world at the time; it serves as the engine that drives much of the Golden Age; the Arabian Nights collection of stories and legends.

programme.title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
programme.sub-title: The Arab World's Greatest Writer: al-Jahiz
programme.desc: Considered by many scholars to be the finest writer of Arabic prose to ever live, Al-Jahiz is a stylist and author of more than 200 works, uncovering the origins of Arabic writing and documenting the life and works of Al-Jahiz.

programme.title: Between Cross and Crescent: Jewish Civilization from Mohammed to Spinoza
programme.desc: Some preliminary observations about Jewish history; the landlessness that has applied for most of it; the approach taken with material often laden with ideological presuppositions.

programme.title: Between Cross and Crescent: Jewish Civilization from Mohammed to Spinoza
programme.sub-title: The Rabbinic Legacy prior to Islam
programme.desc: The destruction of the Jerusalem Temple by the Babylonians; the transfer of large numbers of Jews to Babylonia; new sectarian groups seek to interpret Jewish life and promote their own claims to leadership; the destruction of the second Temple.

programme.title: Between Cross and Crescent: Jewish Civilization from Mohammed to Spinoza
programme.sub-title: The Beginnings of Jewish Life under Islam
programme.desc: The rise of Mohammed's new religion in the seventh century; the cultural environment under which Jews lived in the Middle East and in the Iberian Peninsula is transformed; early Islam is in dialogue with the Jewish tradition from its very inception.

programme.title: Between Cross and Crescent: Jewish Civilization from Mohammed to Spinoza
programme.desc: The institutions that govern Jewish life in Baghdad; the structure of and threats to rabbinic power and the complex system of Jewish communal autonomy existing outside of Baghdad and stretching throughout the Middle East, North Africa, and beyond.

programme.title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
programme.sub-title: Religious Conflict in the Roman World

programme.title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
programme.sub-title: Gods and Their Cities in the Roman Empire
programme.desc: How are pagan gods worshiped in ancient Rome; using evidence both literary and archaeological, grasping the diverse assortment of religious practices in an empire that ranges from Britain to Egypt; comprising a fifth of the world's population.

programme.title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
programme.desc: Rome's first emperor, Augustus, establishes an institution to venerate an emperor's spirit; which then resides as a god on Mount Olympus; how emperors take pains to deify their predecessors to position themselves next among that honored line.

programme.title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
programme.desc: Mystery cults are believed to be the worship of a particular god; they involve the choice to join and undergo an initiation rite. Some scholars maintain that specific cults form a bridge between paganism and Christianity.

programme.title: The Holy Land Revealed
